title: Molecular Cloud Populations in the Context of Their Host Galaxy Environments: A Multiwavelength Perspective
question: How do molecular cloud populations depend on local and global properties of the host galaxy, and what are the characteristic timescales relevant to molecular cloud evolution and star formation across 80 PHANGS-ALMA galaxies?

what.value: PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) imaging data products (v4) and global galaxy properties

evidence.quote: We use the PHANGS–ALMA $\mathrm{CO}\,(2\text{--}1)$ imaging data[^1] (cite: Leroy_etal_2021a) to probe molecular gas properties on ${\lesssim}150$ pc scales.
These global properties are measured by (cite: Leroy_etal_2021a) for all PHANGS-ALMA galaxies.
We extract a set of molecular gas measurements for each object tabulated in the PHANGS–ALMA CPROPS catalogs[^2] (cite: Rosolowsky_etal_2021).

what.value: Rotation curves, inclination angles, and position angles derived from CO line kinematics

evidence.quote: We use rotation curves derived from CO line kinematics by (cite: Lang_etal_2020) to characterize galactic orbital kinematics (e.g., orbital period and shear) locally within each galaxy.
Table notes: (2) distance (cite: Anand_etal_2020); (3) inclination angle (cite: Lang_etal_2020); (4) position angle (cite: Lang_etal_2020);

what.value: Morphological environment masks constructed from near-IR images

evidence.quote: We use the environment masks presented in (cite: Querejeta_etal_2021) to distinguish different morphological regions in each galaxy.
Table notes: (2) distance (cite: Anand_etal_2020);

what.value: Spitzer IRAC 3.6 um images from the S4G survey

evidence.quote: For 61 galaxies in our sample, we use *Spitzer* IRAC $3.6$ $\mu$m images from the S$^4$G survey (cite: Sheth_etal_2010).

what.value: WISE and GALEX images from the z0MGS project

evidence.quote: For those without S$^4$G data, we instead use *WISE* W1 band ($3.4$ $\mu$m) images compiled by the $z0$MGS project (cite: Leroy_etal_2019).

what.value: Archival HI 21 cm data from THINGS, VIVA, HERACLES, LVHIS, and literature

evidence.quote: The other galaxies have archival data from either large nearby galaxy surveys such as THINGS (cite: Walter_etal_2008), VIVA (cite: Chung_etal_2009), HERACLES (cite: Leroy_etal_2009), LVHIS (cite: Koribalski_etal_2018)

recipe.goal: Derive individual molecular cloud and pixel-level physical properties
recipe.method: Extract object-by-object properties from PHANGS-ALMA CPROPS catalogs and pixel-by-pixel properties from strict CO(2-1) moment maps at 60, 90, 120, and 150 pc resolutions, applying inclination corrections.
assumptions: Fiducial metallicity-dependent conversion factor alpha_CO(1-0) = 4.35 * Z'^-1.6 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1
Molecular gas disk thickness H = 100 pc
Inclination correction of cos(i) for surface density and (cos(i))^0.5 for velocity dispersion

recipe.goal: Aggregate cloud and environmental properties in kpc-scale apertures and correct for completeness
recipe.method: Divide each galaxy into 1.5 kpc hexagonal apertures (and 500 pc radial bins). Compute mass-weighted ensemble averages of cloud properties, clumping factor, and area-weighted local environmental metrics. Apply lognormal PDF completeness corrections.
key_parameters: Hexagonal aperture spacing = 1.5 kpc (projected area 1.95 kpc^2), out to r_gal = 1.5 r_25
assumptions: Intrinsic CO intensity distribution within each aperture follows a lognormal distribution above a sharp intensity threshold
Optically thin HI 21 cm emission with 35% helium/heavy elements contribution
Chabrier IMF for UV+MIR SFR and global stellar mass; Kroupa IMF for Halpha+MIR SFR
Global mass-metallicity relation with a fixed radial metallicity gradient of -0.1 dex/r_e

recipe.goal: Characterize pairwise correlations and perform variable selection for predictive models
recipe.method: Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficients and variance inflation factors (VIFs) across 871 high-completeness apertures, then perform multivariable linear regression in log space using Lasso regression and BIC model selection.
key_parameters: Subsample selection: 871 apertures from 42 galaxies with f_flux > 0.5 and f_area > 0.2
Noise variance sigma^2 = 0.1 dex^2 for M, R, Sigma, sigma; sigma^2 = 0.25 dex^2 for P_turb and alpha_vir; model selection threshold Delta BIC <= 10
assumptions: Gaussian error in logarithmic space for BIC calculation

recipe.goal: Estimate characteristic timescales of molecular cloud evolution and star formation
recipe.method: Calculate mass-weighted harmonic mean free-fall time, turbulence crossing time, and cloud-cloud collision time, alongside orbital time, shearing time, and molecular gas depletion time across apertures, and compute Spearman rank correlations with depletion time.
assumptions: Spherical symmetry for free-fall time calculation
Shear-induced cloud-cloud collision model with random spatial distribution of clouds on adjacent circular orbits

answer_key.quantity: Environmental surface density of molecular gas (disk, aperture-weighted)

evidence.quote: Weighting all apertures in galaxy disks equally, we find typical surface densities of $\Sigma_\mathrm{\star}=65^{+80}_{-34}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ and $\Sigma_\mathrm{mol}=5.4^{+10.8}_{-3.7}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ (panels *e* and *f*).

answer_key.quantity: Environmental surface density of molecular gas (disk, molecular gas mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: we find that most molecular gas mass resides in environments with even higher surface densities ($\Sigma_\mathrm{\star}=110^{+140}_{-60}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$, $\Sigma_\mathrm{mol}=17^{+29}_{-11}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$, $\Sigma_\mathrm{gas}=28^{+30}_{-15}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$)

answer_key.quantity: Environmental SFR surface density (disk, aperture-weighted)

evidence.quote: The typical range of SFR surface density of “disk” apertures, when weighted by simple number counts, is $\Sigma_\mathrm{SFR}=3.5^{+6.8}_{-2.1}\times10^{-3}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~yr^{-1}~kpc^{-2}$}$ (panel *h*).

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average molecular cloud mass at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: The mass-weighted average molecular cloud mass at 150 pc resolution is $6.9^{+10.5}_{-4.5}\times10^6~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot$}$ for all clouds in galaxy disks (panel *a*).

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average molecular cloud 3D radius at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: the mass-weighted cloud effective radius measured at the same resolution spans $90^{+19}_{-15}$ pc, which slightly exceeds half the beam FWHM size (panel *b*).

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average molecular cloud surface density at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: At 150 pc resolution, the mass-weighted molecular cloud surface density in galaxy disks is $78^{+124}_{-50}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ from the object-based approach and $33^{+60}_{-22}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ from the pixel-based approach

answer_key.quantity: Pixel-based average molecular cloud surface density at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: At 150 pc resolution, the mass-weighted molecular cloud surface density in galaxy disks is $78^{+124}_{-50}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ from the object-based approach and $33^{+60}_{-22}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ from the pixel-based approach

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average molecular cloud surface density at 150 pc (center/bar, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: Compared to the results for disk apertures, the cloud populations in galaxy centers and stellar bars have much higher mass-weighted mean surface densities of $210^{+560}_{-160}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ (object-based) or $200^{+840}_{-160}~\mbox{$\rm M_\odot~pc^{-2}$}$ (pixel-based).

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average velocity dispersion at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: For molecular cloud populations located in galaxy disks, we find mass-weighted average velocity dispersions of $5.8^{+1.9}_{-1.5}~\mbox{$\rm km~s^{-1}$}$ (object-based; panel *e*) or $4.7^{+2.2}_{-1.7}~\mbox{$\rm km~s^{-1}$}$ (pixel-based; panel *i*).

answer_key.quantity: Pixel-based average velocity dispersion at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: For molecular cloud populations located in galaxy disks, we find mass-weighted average velocity dispersions of $5.8^{+1.9}_{-1.5}~\mbox{$\rm km~s^{-1}$}$ (object-based; panel *e*) or $4.7^{+2.2}_{-1.7}~\mbox{$\rm km~s^{-1}$}$ (pixel-based; panel *i*).

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average turbulent pressure at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: Molecular clouds in galaxy disks have mass-weighted average turbulent pressure of $2.1^{+7.2}_{-1.6}\times10^5~\mbox{$\rm K~cm^{-3}$}$ (object-based; panel *f*) or $1.1^{+5.4}_{-0.9}\times10^5~\mbox{$\rm K~cm^{-3}$}$ (pixel-based; panel *j*).

answer_key.quantity: Object-based average virial parameter at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: Molecular cloud populations in galaxy disks exhibit a narrow range of mass-weighted average virial parameters: $1.1^{+0.8}_{-0.4}$ (object-based; panel *g*) or $1.6^{+0.9}_{-0.6}$ (pixel-based; panel *k*).

answer_key.quantity: Pixel-based average virial parameter at 150 pc (disk, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: Molecular cloud populations in galaxy disks exhibit a narrow range of mass-weighted average virial parameters: $1.1^{+0.8}_{-0.4}$ (object-based; panel *g*) or $1.6^{+0.9}_{-0.6}$ (pixel-based; panel *k*).

answer_key.quantity: Completeness-corrected molecular gas clumping factor at 150 pc (all apertures, mass-weighted)

evidence.quote: We find a completeness-corrected clumping factor of $1.9^{+1.1}_{-0.4}$ (uniform weight per aperture) or $1.9^{+1.0}_{-0.4}$ (weighted by molecular gas mass in each aperture) across our sample (panel *c*).

score_reason: The paper provides complete, explicit mathematical equations for every derived quantity, correction factor, and statistical model, releases the open-source MegaTable v3.0 code on GitHub/Zenodo, and publishes the full machine-readable tables on CANFAR. Reproduction of all statistical distributions, correlations, Lasso/BIC models, and timescale analyses from the published tables is completely straightforward; only rebuilding the table from scratch is slightly limited by a few 'in prep' ancillary maps/catalogs.
rediscovery_reason: The complete multiwavelength aperture database is publicly archived, the analysis pipeline and formulas (completeness corrections, inclination corrections, Spearman correlations, LassoLarsIC variable selection, and timescale derivations) are fully specified, and all key results are quantitative and tabulated.
